declarations.checkedType: agent(body: string, key: string, summary: string) -> string with exclusive
declarations.documentation:
Tool: save a note to your persistent memory under a short key (e.g. "user/name",
"prefs/timezone"). @summary@ is one line shown back to you every turn in the memory index; @body@ is
the full note, read on demand with recall. Both survive restarts, so save durable facts, preferences
and decisions rather than this turn's scratch work; re-using a key overwrites it, and always write a
real summary — one that identifies the note, not one that reproduces it, since recall and search still
reach the body and a summary past one line is cut in the index anyway.
declarations.name: remember

parameters.label: body

declarations.documentation:
Tool: delete a memory by its key, removing both its index summary and its body — use it to prune
stale or wrong facts. The answer says which of two things happened: `forgot`, the memory was there and
is now gone; `was_absent`, nothing was stored under that key and nothing was deleted. Read it before
you tell anyone a note is gone — a mistyped key removes nothing — and call list_memories to see your
keys.

declarations.checkedType: agent(pattern: string) -> string with delete | get | list | set
declarations.documentation:
Tool: search your persistent memory for a pattern — the way to find a note you remember the content
of but not the key. @pattern@ is plain text, not a regular expression and not a query language: it
matches wherever it occurs as a substring, case is ignored ("docker" finds "Docker"), and it reads
the full body of every saved note, so it finds what a one-line summary left out. Each match comes back
as its `- key: summary` line plus a short excerpt; a cut excerpt and any matches beyond the ones shown
are always stated outright, so read a note in full with recall(key) and narrow the pattern when told
there is more — matches arrive in stored key order, not by relevance, and nothing is written.
declarations.name: search

parameters.documentation: Plain text to look for, matched as a substring anywhere in a key, a summary or a note body; case is ignored.
parameters.label: pattern
